newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium takes steps to help the poor.
newsitem.headline: Belgium takes steps to help the poor.

text.p: Belgium on Wednesday announced a string of measures to help tens of thousands living below the poverty line, including extending national health care to the poor. "These are important steps," Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene told a news conference after the weekly cabinet meeting.

He added the package, worth a total of about 700 million francs ($19.7 million), would have no impact on the 1997 budget deficit since the measures had on the whole been anticipated when the budget was drawn up in September last year.

A key plank of the package -- aimed at improving living conditions for some six percent of the population, or an estimated 600,000 Belgians -- is including the poorest, many of them homeless, in the national health care system.

Job opportunities for the poor are being improved so that people no longer suffer the loss of part of their benefits when they find part-time work. Employers may also use social security benefits to meet part of their labour costs.
State Secretary for Social Integration Jan Peeters said the number of poor in Belgium was one of the lowest in Europe thanks to the country's extensive social security system.

He said that over the last 20 years the number of poor had remained relatively stable, but there had been a shift in the composition with the proportion of under-35s rising and the number of pensioners falling as the pension system was improved.
The latest measures include a guaranteed minimum income for pensioners.
